handoff.purpose: Define core data structures (WriteAttempt, CheckPolicy) and baseline checks (parses, not_truncated, no_elision, not_substituted) for write lanes.

symbols.name: WriteAttempt
symbols.note: Dataclass holding rel, proposed, repo_root, original, creating; provides is_python property.

symbols.name: CheckPolicy
symbols.note: Dataclass with elision_markers, min_size_ratio, min_symbol_survival, min_symbols_to_judge, first_party_roots, max_named_imports.

symbols.name: toplevel_defs
symbols.note: Returns frozenset of top-level function/class names, or None if source does not parse.

symbols.name: _module_path
symbols.note: Resolves dotted module name to Path, checking .py file, __init__.py, or namespace directory with .py files.

symbols.name: _exports
symbols.note: Returns (frozenset of names, opaque bool) from a Python file; opaque if star-import or module-level __getattr__.

symbols.name: parses
symbols.note: Checks that proposed content is parseable Python; returns refusal string if not.

symbols.name: not_truncated
symbols.note: Checks that proposed length is at least min_size_ratio of original; returns refusal if too short.

symbols.name: no_elision
symbols.note: Checks for new elision markers in proposed text; returns refusal if found.

symbols.name: not_substituted
symbols.note: Checks that top-level definitions in proposed file overlap with original; truncated in this chunk.

claims.text: A check returns '' to pass and a human-readable reason to refuse
claims.why: All baseline check functions (parses, not_truncated, no_elision, not_substituted) return '' on pass and a non-empty string on refusal.

claims.text: a check that RAISES is treated as a refusal
claims.why: The chunk does not contain the run_checks function that would handle exceptions.

claims.text: Every function here was lifted, not written: each one is a guard that already existed in providers/deepseek.py
claims.why: No code from providers/deepseek.py is present in this chunk.

claims.text: the first four arguments are bundled into WriteAttempt
claims.why: WriteAttempt contains rel, proposed, repo_root, original (and creating).

claims.text: Two of the baseline checks need a fifth fact (is this file being CREATED, so that there is no original to compare against)
claims.why: not_truncated and not_substituted use attempt.creating to skip checks when creating is True.

claims.text: keeping the two facts separate rather than inferring 'creating' from an empty original matters: a lane that truncates a real file to nothing must not be able to present that as a creation and skip the guards that only run on edits.
claims.why: WriteAttempt has both original (default '') and creating (default False) as separate fields.

claims.text: Only refused when the marker is NEW, so a file that legitimately contains the phrase does not become unwritable.
claims.why: no_elision checks that the marker is in proposed.lower() and not in original.lower().

claims.text: Below this fraction of the original size, a 'full rewrite' is a truncation.
Below this fraction of surviving top-level definitions, a 'rewrite' is a different file rather than an edited one.
claims.why: The not_substituted function is truncated; the survival ratio logic is not fully visible.

claims.text: Below this many top-level definitions the survival ratio is noise -- losing one of two functions is an ordinary edit.
claims.why: The not_substituted function is truncated; the logic using min_symbols_to_judge is not fully visible.

claims.text: Import roots that belong to THIS repository. A missing third-party package is an environment question and none of this gate's business; a missing first-party module is a file the model invented.
claims.why: The imports_resolve function is not defined in this chunk; its behavior cannot be verified.

claims.text: Only the TOP level: a rewrite is free to reorganise nested helpers, and counting those would make ordinary refactors look like substitutions.
claims.why: toplevel_defs only collects names from ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef, ast.ClassDef at the top level of tree.body.

claims.text: A directory WITHOUT __init__.py still counts. Since Python 3.3 such a directory is an implicit namespace package (PEP 420) and imports perfectly well -- tools and tests in this repository are exactly that, and both import fine while reporting __file__ is None.
claims.why: _module_path returns the directory if it exists and contains any .py file, without requiring __init__.py.

claims.text: The returned directory is deliberately not a readable module: _exports fails closed on it (an OSError becomes opaque=True), which is the honest answer, because what a namespace package provides is its submodules and no single file lists them.

Runs on CREATED files too, which is where the hole was: an edit that stops parsing was caught by not_substituted as a side effect, but a brand-new module that does not parse had nothing looking at it -- the imports check returns early on a parse failure, calling it 'a different guard's business'. This is that guard.
claims.why: parses does not check attempt.creating; it runs on all Python files. It returns early only if toplevel_defs succeeds or if original is already unparsable.

claims.text: The classic full-rewrite failure: the model returned part of the file.
claims.why: not_truncated compares lengths and refuses if proposed is too short.

claims.text: Only NEW markers count. A file that already contained the phrase would otherwise become permanently unwritable by this lane.
claims.why: no_elision checks that the marker is in proposed.lower() and not in original.lower().

claims.text: Deliberately Python-only. The check needs a parser to be meaningful, and a guess about other languages would either fire on ordinary edits or provide false assurance for files it cannot actually read.
claims.why: not_substituted returns '' if not attempt.is_python or attempt.creating.

observations.what: not_substituted function is truncated mid-sentence; the full logic is not visible in this chunk.
parses has a redundant ast.parse call after toplevel_defs already parsed the source.
_exports considers a module opaque if it has a star-import or module-level __getattr__, but may miss other dynamic mechanisms (e.g., __import__, importlib).
not_truncated uses policy.min_size_ratio, default 0.5. A file that is exactly 50% of original size passes; a file at 49.9% fails. This is likely intentional but could be sensitive to rounding.
